thread.title: Stock Market Update: Netflix Helps Fuel Intraday Rebound

title: Stock Market Update: Netflix Helps Fuel Intraday Rebound
text:
Netflix Helps Fuel Intraday Rebound 17-Jul-18 13:05 ET Dow +61.50 at 25125.86, Nasdaq +42.07 at 7847.80, S&P +11.75 at 2809.92
[BRIEFING.COM] The stock market got off to a slow start this morning, but has been climbing steadily throughout the session. The major averages are now in positive territory, hovering near their best marks of the day. The S&P 500 is up 0.4% after being down as much as 0.3%. The Nasdaq is up 0.6%, and the Dow is up 0.2%.
Netflix (NFLX 380.82, -19.66) has helped fuel today's reversal, cutting its loss from 14.1% to 5.0%. Shares initially sold off after the streaming media company reported Q2 subscriber growth well below estimates, but better-than-expected earnings and upgrades at BMO Capital Markets and Stifel have helped keep losses in check. Other FAANG names -- including Facebook (FB 208.96, +1.73) Apple (AAPL 191.22, +0.31), Amazon (AMZN 1843.55, +21.08), and Alphabet (GOOG 1201.00, +17.14) -- have followed Netflix's lead.
The information technology sector, which houses most of the aforementioned names, is up 0.7% this afternoon, extending its monthly gain to 5.0%. The lightly-weighted materials space (+1.3%) is the top-performing group, and consumer staples (+0.8%) are also relatively strong.
Within the health care space, 129.13, +4.44) is up 3.6% after reporting better-than-expected earnings and revenues for the second quarter, but UnitedHealth (UNH 249.63, -7.35) is down 2.9% despite also beating bottom-line estimates.
Elsewhere, the heavily-weighted financial sector (+0.3%) is trailing the broader market a bit, with Goldman Sachs (GS 228.099, -3.36) down 1.5%. The investment bank beat earnings estimates on better-than-expected revenues this morning. Conversely, Charles Schwab (SCHW 52.70, +1.64) is up 3.2% after beating bottom-line estimates.
Utilities (unch), telecom services (unch), and real estate (-0.4%) are the worst-performing groups and the only groups currently in negative territory. The energy space (unch) is just slightly higher, but has been underperforming all day as crude oil struggles to bounce back from yesterday's tumble. WTI crude futures are currently down 0.2% at $67.93 per barrel, but were down as much as 2.5% earlier.
In the bond market, U.S. Treasuries are mostly flat, although the Fed-sensitive 2-yr note is showing relative weakness, pushing its yield up one basis point to 2.61%. Meanwhile, the yield on the benchmark 10-yr Treasury note is unchanged at 2.86%.
Fed Chair Jerome Powell gave his semi-annual testimony today, but there weren't any new revelations; Mr. Powell reiterated the need for gradual rate hikes amid a strengthening economy.
